Hon'ble Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.
Ms. Kajri Gupta, counsel for the
revisionist.
2. Mr. Deepak Bisht, learned Deputy A.G.
for the State.
3. Ms. Sarita Bisht, learned counsel for
respondent no.2.
4. The present criminal revision petition has
been filed challenging the impugned judgment
and order dated 18.05.2023 passed by the
learned Judge, Family Court, Kashipur, District
Udham Singh Nagar whereby the application
under Section 125 Cr.P.C. (the criminal
procedure then was) filed by revisionist was
partly allowed and a maintenance amount of
₹20,000/- per month was awarded in favour of
the revisionist/minor daughter of the respondent
no.2. The revisionist seeks enhancement of the
said maintenance.
5. Learned counsel for the parties have
submitted that in compliance with the directions
of this Court dated 24.03.2025 both parties
appeared before the Mediator appointed by the
Member Secretary, Uttarakhand State Legal
Services Authority for mediation proceedings
held on different dates.
He would further submit that the
mediation proceedings were successful and the
parties have amicably resolved their dispute on
mutually agreed terms and conditions as
recorded in the settlement/agreement dated
05.05.2025, in Mediation Case No. 21 of 2025
titled Riya vs. State of Uttarakhand & another,
before the Mediation Centre, Nainital.
6. In view of the amicable settlement and
considering that both parties have agreed to
abide by the terms of the compromise, this Court
is of the considered view that no useful purpose

2025:UHC:4239
would be served by keeping the present revision
pending.
7. Accordingly, the criminal revision
petition is disposed of in terms of the
settlement/agreement dated 05.05.2025 which
shall form part of this order.
8. Pending applications, if any, also stand
disposed of.
(Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.)
 21.05.2025
Mamta
